overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: an in-person meeting at an accessible location did not require remote access, and the disputed Zoom waiting-room claim could not be resolved on the evidence, so no finding was made. A reminder about prompt admission from waiting rooms was given, but no order issued.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board's March 11 meeting lacked adequate alternative remote access because Zoom participants were removed and readmitted every 40 minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board held its March 11 meeting in-person at a location that was physically open and accessible to the public, the Board was not required to provide a method of alternative remote access to the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged he was kept in the Zoom waiting room for at least fifteen minutes at the start of the March 11 meeting and was not admitted.
allegations.key_passage: Because the screenshot does not include a date or timestamp showing when Mr. Nardi was waiting to be admitted to the Zoom meeting, we are unable to resolve this factual dispute and therefore make no findings as to whether Mr. Nardi was individually excluded from joining the Board’s March 11 meeting.
